comment: src/RAM40964.cpp at commit b90cd69. What a data output carries is whatever was written into that cell, so its range is the range of what was put there rather than a property of the module; the 0V to 10V given is what the module's own write path produces. The address knobs are added to the jacks and the sum is wrapped into the grid rather than clamped (src/Utility.cpp line 101), so an address running off one edge reappears on the other. fillAddressArray also has a second behaviour worth knowing: with a Y jack patched and an X jack empty, the X address is the knob alone; with an X jack patched and a Y jack empty, the X voltage is read as a position through the whole 4096 cells rather than across one row. The four per-plane write switches take three positions, and the middle one lets an expander write while the module's own jacks cannot. The panel prints W and R either side of Address and either side of Data, WE against the write-enable switches, +64, +1 and +0 against the increment switch, HSV, RGB and P3 against the display switch, Write and Clear, and Phasor over the phasor jack. The 4096 lamps of the display are light widgets with no parameters, so none can be clicked for help.
